title: Apple Unveils Its First Touchscreen Laptop
paragraphs: For years, Apple dismissed the idea of touchscreen laptops. In 2010, co-founder Steve Jobs called them "ergonomically terrible." Two years later, then-CEO Tim Cook compared combining a laptop and a tablet to putting a toaster and a refrigerator together.
"Yes, for the very first time, we are bringing touch to the Mac," Apple CEO John Ternus announced at an event in Los Angeles on October 28.
The new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display comes in 14-inch and 16-inch versions, with US prices starting at $2,899 and $3,399 respectively.

Users can still control it with a keyboard and trackpad, but can now also scroll through webpages, pinch to zoom in on photos, drag slides between presentations and move windows around with their fingers.
Apple says many existing apps will work with the touchscreen immediately because the software automatically treats taps as mouse clicks.

The technology could be particularly useful for creative professionals. Graphic designers can draw directly on the screen, musicians can play virtual instruments, and app developers can test touch controls in iPhone and iPad apps.
Touchscreen laptops have been around for over a decade. While early models were often bulky and awkward to use, the technology has since improved significantly.

The market is growing, too. According to research firm IDC, around 33.4 million touchscreen laptops were shipped worldwide in 2025, up 22% from the previous year. However, they still accounted for only 16% of all laptop shipments.
And Apple is no stranger to entering a market late. It wasn't the first to introduce MP3 players, tablets or smartwatches, but helped popularize them through simpler, more intuitive designs.

The touchscreen MacBook is the latest in a series of products announced since Ternus became CEO in September. Under the former head of hardware engineering, Apple has also unveiled the foldable iPhone Duo and HomeView, a smart-home hub.
The new MacBook Pro is now available for pre-order and will go on sale on November 6.
